keywords.def: sun letters: the laam of al- is not said, the next letter doubles
moon letters: the laam of al- is said clearly
the sign that doubles a letter

questions.q: Read «وَإِلَى ٱلْجِبَالِ» (88:19). Is the laam said?
questions.a: Yes: jeem is a moon letter, so al-jibaal with a clear laam.

questions.q: Sun and moon sort (pupil PDF): sort 12 al- words from Surahs 88, 96 and 97. Today's rota group recites 88:12 to 16 in turn.
questions.a: Sun: ٱلسَّمَآءِ, ٱلنَّاصِيَةِ, ٱلرُّوحُ, ٱلَّذِى, ٱلرُّجْعَىٰٓ, ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ. Moon: ٱلْإِبِلِ, ٱلْجِبَالِ, ٱلْأَرْضِ, ٱلْقَدْرِ, ٱلْفَجْرِ, ٱلْقَلَمِ.

questions.q: Extend: write the moon-letter phrase from memory.
Stretch: why do you think the laam merges into sun letters?
questions.a: Sun letters are made near the laam (tongue tip and front of the mouth), so it merges easily.
A) Sun: as-samaa'. Seen is a sun letter: the laam is not said and the seen has a shaddah.

questions.q: Think again: We say 'ash-shams' (the sun) but 'al-qamar' (the moon). Why does the 'l' sometimes disappear?
questions.a: Before sun letters the laam merges into the next letter (which gets a shaddah); before moon letters it is said clearly.
